Score README.md for AI tells
expected_behavior: runs scripts/slop_lint.py on the file rather than judging by feel
reports the 0-100 score, the band, and the per-metric breakdown with flagged line numbers
explains that flags come from clusters of co-occurring tells, not any single metric
does not rewrite or edit the text

cases.prompt: score this academic abstract for slop: [a 200-word abstract with hedges]
expected_behavior: passes --genre academic so hedge and em-dash thresholds are relaxed
states which genre profile was used in the report
does not flag ordinary academic hedging as slop on its own

cases.prompt: give me a slop score for this tweet: 'Big news — we shipped.'
expected_behavior: notes the text is below the minimum length for a confident score
reports the low-confidence flag from the script instead of inventing a confident number
does not fail or warn on the em dash alone

cases.prompt: wire a slop gate into our docs CI
expected_behavior: uses the script's --fail-above flag and documents the exit-code contract (0 pass, 1 error, 2 threshold exceeded)
recommends a warn-first rollout with the documented default threshold rather than inventing a strict cutoff
mentions thresholds are genre-aware and configurable

cases.prompt: scan this human-written essay that uses lots of em dashes for AI patterns
expected_behavior: reports the em-dash rate but does not conclude AI involvement from dashes alone
states the cluster rule and the wide human em-dash range explicitly
never frames the result as proof of authorship or an accusation
